clue.text: It's usually tricky learning English

indicators.note: tricky means intricate or awkward, so the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A student remarks that picking up the English language is generally a hard business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges LEARNING plus E; 'It's' simply leads into the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe what happens as a rule, on most occasions, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Urge Prime Minister to wear a garland on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the minister wears the garland, so the garland goes round him

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers

explanation.surface: Someone presses the PM to put on a flower garland as they climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wear' and 'on the way up' are both indicators: the garland goes round the minister, then the whole is read upwards since this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or urge someone forward.

clue.text: Act quickly to secure first class

parts.note: to get is to obtain or secure
cracking is British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Advice to move fast to win a top-grade ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: To get cracking is an idiom meaning to start work at once and move fast.

clue.text: About 16 votes against advertisements

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is placed round the other

parts.note: noes are votes against a motion
16-across is a jerk or spasm, a tic

explanation.surface: A tally of opposing votes on something numbered sixteen.
explanation.walkthrough: A number alone refers to another answer: '16' stands for 16-across, used here through a synonym. 'About' is the container indicator, not a word meaning roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: Notices are announcements put up or printed, like advertisements.

clue.text: A torrid — a sizzling heater

indicators.note: something sizzling is hot and agitated, so the letters jump into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A breathless description of a heater as scorching hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sizzling' rearranges A TORRID A.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiator is a device for heating a room.

clue.text: Scholar visiting cricket ground turned up to have a bowl

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the letters are read upwards
a visitor goes inside, so the scholar is put inside the ground

parts.note: the Oval is a London cricket ground
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate or scholar

explanation.surface: A graduate visits a cricket ground and turns up hoping to bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visiting' puts BA in OVAL to give OBAVAL, and 'turned up' reverses it. THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; 'bowl' looks like cricket but is a basin.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavabo is a washbasin, a bowl for washing the hands, especially in church ritual.

clue.text: Surrounded by love, good man trembled

indicators.note: something that trembled is shaken about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A good man, encircled by affection, is left shaking with emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trembled' shakes up O, G and MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To be among things is to be in their midst, with them on every side.

clue.text: You'll find us in halls in the country

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: atria are entrance halls, the plural of atrium
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tour guide promises to meet visitors in the halls of a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container indicator; 'You'll find' just links. Halls here are grand entrance spaces, plural of atrium.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a country in central Europe.

clue.text: Gold and black symbol of power

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Gold and black regalia represent royal authority.
explanation.definitionFit: The orb carried by a monarch is an emblem of sovereign power.

clue.text: Martial artist of restricted development?

definitions.meaning: a person of intermediate rank in judo or karate, named after the coloured belt worn
land round a town where building is limited by planning law

explanation.surface: A fighter in a judo class who is still not fully grown.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a green belt is protected countryside around a city where new building is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a mid-level grade in martial arts and a protected zone where construction is restricted.

clue.text: Insignificant amount of training given to bird

parts.note: PE is physical education, a session of physical training at school
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird gets only a tiny dose of exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Petit, borrowed from French, means small or minor, as in petit point or petty matters.

clue.text: What 501, as you can see, is — by 167

definitions.text: What 501, as you can see, is — by 167

parts.note: in Roman numerals D is 500 and I is 1, so 501 is DI
something you can see is visible

explanation.surface: A piece of arithmetic: 501 divided by 167 comes out exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: 501 is three times 167, so the whole clue is the definition, while 501 in Roman numerals plus 'as you can see' builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A number that can be split by another with no remainder is said to be divisible by it; 3 x 167 = 501.

clue.text: Surprisingly ill-bred monarch, a man in charge at palace

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests something turned out in an unexpected form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Courtiers are shocked that the royal is so rude, while one official runs the palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges ILLBRED MONARCH A. The LORD CHAMBERLAIN is the senior officer of the British royal household.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Chamberlain is the chief official of the royal household, running affairs at the palace.

clue.text: A King, a Pope and I pooled together to make ill-considered purchase

indicators.note: pooled together means mixed into one pool, so all these letters are blended

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch, a pontiff and the speaker club together to buy something rashly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pooled together' mixes AKINGAPOPE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To buy a pig in a poke is an idiom for purchasing something without inspecting it first.

clue.text: I'm loaded —- but money's stolen

parts.note: money is bucks, slang for dollars
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A rich person protests that their fortune was all taken by thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm loaded' suggests wealth, but it is a gun's charge speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot of small lead pellets is what a shotgun is loaded with, so the ammunition can say it is loaded.

clue.text: Bumboat woman found in meadow

definitions.meaning: Little ... is the bumboat woman in Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore
a yellow wild flower common in grassland

explanation.surface: A woman who sells goods from a boat is discovered in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: A bumboat is a small boat selling provisions to ships; the character comes from the operetta HMS Pinafore.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both an operetta character who sells from a boat and a common yellow meadow flower.

clue.text: Ill-will shown by married woman

parts.note: Alice is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A wife displays spite.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the desire to harm others, which is the same as ill-will or spite.

clue.text: The croc I shot — an indirect hit

indicators.note: shot can mean ruined or blasted apart, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A hunter boasts of shooting a crocodile, though the bullet glanced off something first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges THECROCI; it looks like the hunter's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A ricochet is a shot that rebounds off a surface before striking, so an indirect hit.

clue.text: Fool attending church, the jerk!

parts.note: a twit is a silly fool

explanation.surface: Someone scolds an idiot who has turned up at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' reads as an insult for the fool but means a sudden spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitch is a sudden involuntary movement, a jerk of a muscle.

clue.text: Conservative charm, though heartless, is most important

indicators.note: heartless means losing the heart, so the middle letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to enthral is to charm or captivate

explanation.surface: A Tory's charm, though cold, is said to be what matters most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes H, the middle letter of ENTHRAL, leaving ENTRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Central can mean principal or of chief importance, as in a central issue.

clue.text: Put one's finger on something sharp

definitions.meaning: to identify something exactly, to locate it precisely
the point of a pin, a very sharp tip

explanation.surface: Someone touches a sharp object with their finger.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinpoint is to identify precisely, and the noun is literally the sharp tip of a pin.

clue.text: Cat reveals first trace of pollen on pollen container

indicators.note: first trace of picks out just the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the anther is the part of a flower's stamen that holds pollen

explanation.surface: A cat's fur shows a dusting of pollen from a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a big cat, a leopard or similar.

clue.text: Key part of this landscape

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An important element of the view in front of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like an adjective meaning crucial, but it is a low island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A key, or cay, is a small low island or reef.

clue.text: Give encouragement, with kiss, to people in balancing act

parts.note: to egg on is to urge or encourage
and means together with
to spoon is old-fashioned for kissing and cuddling
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A performer is cheered on and kissed by onlookers while balancing.
explanation.walkthrough: The EGG-AND-SPOON RACE is a British school sports day event where runners carry an egg balanced on a spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitors in the race must balance an egg on a spoon while running, so it is a balancing act.

clue.text: Over time, stick up for order

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second
in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick

explanation.surface: After a while someone stands up for orderly conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CANE into ENAC, and 'Over' sets it above T.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact is to decree or order something by law.

clue.text: Bird, fish or insect?

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A naturalist puzzles over what kind of creature they are looking at.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockroach is a common scavenging insect.

clue.text: Coward cut short

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the last letter of the word is taken off

parts.note: curt means short or abrupt

explanation.surface: A coward's escape is brought to an abrupt end.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious reading takes 'cut short' as one phrase; instead 'short' is CURT and 'cut' docks its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a contemptible or cowardly person, originally a mongrel dog.

clue.text: Crocodile's victim given a pipe

parts.note: Captain Hook in Peter Pan is pursued and finally eaten by the crocodile

explanation.surface: Someone eaten by a crocodile is handed a pipe to smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooka, usually spelt hookah, is an oriental water pipe for smoking.

clue.text: Danger of foreign coins being rejected after parking

indicators.note: after places the reversed coins behind the parking letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so the word for the coins is read backwards

parts.note: lire were the coins of Italy

explanation.surface: Someone risks losing their foreign change at a parking meter that refuses it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being rejected' is the reversal indicator and 'after' sets the order; lire were Italy's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril means serious danger or risk.

clue.text: Cleaner gets measure of work —- with a catch in it? On the contrary

indicators.note: the clue first says the catch goes into the unit, then flips it, so the unit goes inside the catch

parts.note: a detent is a catch in a mechanism that stops movement
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A cleaner wonders whether their pay comes with some hidden snag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a catch in it' at face value puts the catch inside the unit; 'On the contrary' flips that, so the unit sits inside the catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a cleaning agent, a substance that cleans.
